questions.question: Which Biology Question Paper Type is given to you?
questions.explanation: This is a paper identification question. The correct answer is Type C as indicated in the paper header.

questions.question: Which of the following characterizes a mature plant cell?

options.A: the cytoplasm fills up the entire cell space
options.B: the nucleus is pushed to the centre of the cell
options.C: the cell wall is made up of cellulose
options.D: the nucleus is small and irregular in shape

questions.explanation: Mature plant cells are characterized by having a cell wall made of cellulose, which provides structural support and protection.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the nucleus of a cell?

options.A: it controls the life processes of the cell
options.B: it translates genetic information for the manufacture of proteins
options.C: it stores and carries hereditary information
options.D: it is reservoir of energy for the cell

questions.explanation: The nucleus is not a reservoir of energy for the cell. Energy storage and production are functions of mitochondria and chloroplasts.

questions.question: The dominant phase in the life cycle of a fern is the?
questions.explanation: In ferns, the sporophyte (the leafy plant we commonly see) is the dominant phase, while the gametophyte is small and inconspicuous.

questions.question: Parental care is exhibited by
questions.explanation: Birds exhibit extensive parental care including nest building, incubation of eggs, and feeding of young.

questions.question: With respect to their decreasing dependence on aquatic conditions for reproduction, which of the following is the correct arrangement of the animals represented?
questions.explanation: The arrangement shows decreasing dependence on water for reproduction, from aquatic animals to fully terrestrial ones.

questions.question: Which of the animals represents the oldest creatures in terms of evolutionary history?
questions.explanation: In evolutionary terms, simpler aquatic organisms appeared earlier than more complex terrestrial ones.

questions.question: Which of the following groups of cells is devoid of true nuclei?
questions.explanation: Viruses are not cellular organisms and lack nuclei. They consist only of genetic material surrounded by a protein coat.

questions.question: The main function of the feathers covering the part labelled I is to

options.A: prevent ectoparasites from attacking the animal
options.B: generate heat to keep the animal warm
options.D: serve as insulator to maintain body heat

questions.explanation: Down feathers serve as insulation to maintain body temperature in birds.

questions.question: Based on the shape and structure of the beak and feet, the bird represented is likely to feed mainly on
questions.explanation: Sharp, hooked beaks and strong talons are adaptations for catching and tearing flesh, characteristic of birds of prey.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of the transverse section of a dicot stem?

options.A: the epidermis is completely encircled by the cortex
options.B: the xylem is more interiorly located than the phloem
options.C: the cambium lies between the cortex and the vascular bundles
options.D: the vascular bundles are randomly scattered within the cortex

questions.explanation: In dicot stems, xylem is located towards the center (interior) while phloem is located towards the outside.

questions.question: The movement of material in the xylem and phloem tissues of the plant are represented by the arrows labelled
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and minerals upward, while phloem transports organic compounds in various directions.

questions.question: During photosynthesis, the arrow labelled II represents the

options.B: absorption of energy from the sun
options.D: release of oxygen as a by-product

questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, oxygen is released as a by-product when water molecules are split.

questions.question: Which of the following is lacking in the diet of a person with kwashiorkor?
questions.explanation: Kwashiorkor is a form of malnutrition caused by protein deficiency, especially in children.

questions.question: The mode of nutrition of sun dew and bladder wort can be described as
questions.explanation: Sundew and bladderwort are carnivorous plants that exhibit holozoic nutrition by trapping and digesting insects.

questions.question: When the mixture of a food substance and Benedict's solution was warmed, the solution changed from blue to brick-red. This indicates the presence of
questions.explanation: Benedict's test shows a color change from blue to brick-red in the presence of reducing sugars like glucose.

questions.question: The primary structure responsible for pumping blood for circulation through the mammalian circulatory system is the
questions.explanation: The left ventricle is the main pumping chamber that forces oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation.

questions.question: Circulation of blood to all parts of the body except the lungs is through
questions.explanation: Systemic circulation carries blood to all body parts except the lungs, which are served by pulmonary circulation.

questions.question: Yeast respires anaerobically to convert simple sugar to carbon(IV) oxide and
questions.explanation: During anaerobic respiration (fermentation), yeast converts sugar to carbon dioxide and ethyl alcohol.

questions.question: The sheet of muscle that separates the thoracic and the abdominal cavities is the
questions.explanation: The diaphragm is a dome-shaped muscle that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity.

questions.question: The oily substance that lubricates the mammalian hair to keep it flexible and water repellent is secreted by the
questions.explanation: Sebaceous glands secrete sebum, an oily substance that lubricates hair and skin.

questions.question: The outer layer of the kidney where the Bowman's capsules are found is the
questions.explanation: The renal cortex is the outer layer of the kidney containing the Bowman's capsules and glomeruli.

questions.question: Which of the following stimuli is likely to elicit a nastic response in an organism?
questions.explanation: Nastic movements are non-directional responses to stimuli, often triggered by chemical substances or touch.

questions.question: In the male reproductive system of a mammal, sperm is stored in the
questions.explanation: The epididymis is where sperm mature and are stored before ejaculation.

questions.question: Chemosynthetic organisms are capable of manufacturing their food from simple inorganic substances through the process of
questions.explanation: Chemosynthetic organisms use energy from chemical reactions, often involving phosphorylation, to produce food.

questions.question: The part of the human gut that has an acidic content is the
questions.explanation: The stomach produces hydrochloric acid, making it the most acidic part of the digestive system.

questions.question: Which of the following structures is correctly matched with the organism in which it is found?
questions.explanation: Contractile vacuoles are found in protozoans and help regulate water balance.

questions.question: A food chain always begins with a
questions.explanation: Food chains always begin with producers (autotrophs) that convert solar energy into chemical energy.

questions.question: Mycorrhizae promote plant growth by

options.A: absorbing inorganic ions from the soil
options.C: helping it to utilize atmospheric nitrogen

questions.explanation: Mycorrhizae are symbiotic fungi that help plants absorb minerals and water from the soil.

questions.question: The barrier between maternal and foetal blood is the
questions.explanation: The placenta acts as a selective barrier allowing exchange of nutrients and waste between maternal and fetal blood.

questions.question: The blood component that has the greatest affinity for oxygen is the
questions.explanation: Erythrocytes (red blood cells) contain hemoglobin which has a high affinity for oxygen.

questions.question: Which of the following organisms is mainly found in the marine habitat?
questions.explanation: Dogfish is a marine shark found in ocean environments.

questions.question: The two halves of the pelvic girdle are joined together at the
questions.explanation: The pubic symphysis is the joint where the two halves of the pelvic girdle meet.

questions.question: Which of the following are ways in which desert animals adapt to extreme heat?
questions.explanation: Desert animals adapt through nocturnal habits and burrowing to avoid extreme heat.

questions.question: Low annual rainfall, sparse vegetation, high diurnal temperatures and cold nights are characteristic features of the
questions.explanation: These characteristics describe the guinea savanna biome found in parts of West Africa.

questions.question: The activity of an organism which affects the survival of another organism in the same habitat constitutes
questions.explanation: Biotic factors involve the interactions between living organisms in an ecosystem.

questions.question: The average number of individuals of a species per unit area of the habitat is the
questions.explanation: Population density is defined as the number of individuals per unit area or volume.

questions.question: The vector for yellow fever is
questions.explanation: Yellow fever is transmitted by Aedes aegypti mosquitoes.

questions.question: The loss of soil through erosion can be reduced by
questions.explanation: Crop rotation helps maintain soil structure and prevents erosion by keeping the soil covered.

questions.question: The protozoan plasmodium falciparum is transmitted by
questions.explanation: Plasmodium falciparum, which causes malaria, is transmitted by female Anopheles mosquitoes.

questions.question: A dilute solution of phenylthiocarbamide tastes bitter to some people and is tasteless to others. This is an example of
questions.explanation: The ability to taste PTC shows discontinuous variation - people either can or cannot taste it.

questions.question: In which plantation are all the trees between the height of 2-4m?
questions.explanation: Based on the diagram, plantation III shows all trees within the 2-4m height range.

questions.question: Which of the following is a true feature of plantation II?

options.A: it has the highest number of trees of about 2m high
options.B: it has highest number of trees
options.C: it has the highest number of tall trees
options.D: the height of all its trees range between 2m and 6m

questions.explanation: From the graph, plantation II shows the highest frequency of trees at approximately 2m height.

questions.question: Thyroxine and adrenalin are examples of hormones which control
questions.explanation: Thyroxine and adrenalin are hormones that influence metabolic rate and behavioral responses.

questions.question: A pair of genes that control a trait is referred to as
questions.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of a gene that control the same trait.

questions.question: The chromosome number of a cell before and after the process of meiosis is conventionally represented as
questions.explanation: Meiosis reduces chromosome number from diploid (2n) to haploid (n).

questions.question: If both parents are heterozygous for a trait, the probability that an offspring will be recessive for that trait is
questions.explanation: In a cross between two heterozygotes (Aa × Aa), the probability of recessive offspring (aa) is 1/4.

questions.question: At what stage in the life history of a mammal is the sex of an individual set?
questions.explanation: Sex is determined at conception when the sperm contributes either an X or Y chromosome.

questions.question: The main distinguishing features between the soldier termite and other members of the caste are the

options.A: presence of wings, possession of a small head and large thorax
options.B: presence of wings, possession of a large thorax and a small head
options.C: absence of wings, possession of strong mandibles and a large head
options.D: absence of wings, possession of big head and the absence of mandible

questions.explanation: Soldier termites are wingless with enlarged heads and strong mandibles for defense.

questions.question: The flippers of a whale and the fins of a fish are examples of
questions.explanation: Whale flippers and fish fins are examples of convergent evolution - similar structures evolved independently for similar functions.
